name: manki-g3-head-slam-grab
notes: Manki ground.3 Head Slam (anim.manki.g3, button 3 in the new numbering), redo to the current GenRA standard, 2026-11-01. The bound clip (manki_ground4_head_slam.anim, session-authored in Codex for PR #271, 2026-10-16) is one of the first GenRA clips. On the v5 'pyro' rig it fails 18 checks: every finger knuckle and middle joint bends backward over ticks 1-33 (up to 110 degrees), both elbows bend backward around the hit, the left wrist folds 128 degrees, the arms snap 69 degrees in one tick at tick 8, the right ankle sinks 6 cm below its idle height during the hit, and it is pose-to-pose (5.8 stops per joint per second, 85% of the joints stopping together, a dead hold over game ticks 10-14 and 35-40). Today's game clock: one 40-tick stage, hitbox on bone.head ticks 10-14 (sphere r 0.5, 14 damage, 28 degrees), IASA 35, a heavy presentation cue at tick 6. The owner allows the frame data to change. This brief authors at 88 ticks, twice a proposed 44-tick game stage: hit from game tick 14 (authored 28) for 5 ticks, IASA game 39 (authored 78). Take B, the developed variant inside the same move identity: he grabs the target's head with both hands and yanks it down into his skull. Take A (manki-g4-head-slam.json) is the literal concept. Keys stage first; the owner approves the key poses before any motion. Rig pack manki-unity-v5 (2026-10-29) is byte-identical to a fresh snapshot of the live MankiRig.prefab taken 2026-11-01 (rig, idle, fall). 2026-11-01 keys runs: the impact target first asked for the head 0.40 m ahead of the hips, which the 0.393 m hips-to-head chain cannot reach; both takes reached 0.38; lowered to 0.36.
character: Manki v5 'pyro' (58 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names, a big head with goggles and a spiky mane, big ears, an open vest and ragged shorts; a two-can spray-can jetpack built into the body mesh and pinned rigidly to Spine2, so it sits on his upper back and turns with the chest; a TORCH-can holster on his left thigh; thumb, index, middle and ring fingers on each hand; arm stretch, forearm offset and fist deform controls that carry the arm skin; a five-joint tail Tail1..5 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest). He is small: hips to head 0.38 m, thigh 0.25 m, shin 0.19 m, upper arm 0.14 m, forearm 0.15 m in this rig. His idle (image 3) is a hunched boxer's crouch: left foot forward, right foot back, knees bent, fists low in front of his hips.
image_notes: 1 and 2: the v5 'pyro' Manki concept the model was built from, front and back. It is a drawing: the rig's proportions rule. 3: the idle on this rig (profile, front, three-quarter rear): the entry and exit pose of this clip.
description:
Manki's ground.3, Head Slam: his heavy grounded normal. He grabs his victim's head with both hands, rears back, then yanks it down into his big skull as he drives it forward and down, like a ram. Whoever stands in front of him gets their head pulled into his. His head is the hitbox (a big sphere on the head joint), so the head's path is the move: it must arrive well out in front of him, on his centre line, travelling fast during the hit. It sends the victim up and away at 28 degrees, so it should feel like a heavy, solid hit: the whole body throws the skull, not just the neck.

Who he is. Manki is a pyromaniac mad-inventor monkey (images 1 and 2): toothy grin with missing teeth, cracked goggles, a burnt brow, a spray-can jetpack on his back. He is small, wiry and a bit unhinged; his head is huge for his body, and he uses it like a battering ram. Character goes into the wind-up and the hit: the grab is greedy and quick, the rear-back a gleeful coil, chin up, grinning at the target. The arms pulling in while the head drives out is what makes the hit read. The recovery is plain.

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind him, so the action must read from behind: the head must leave the silhouette of his back and jetpack and appear out in front and below, not stay hidden behind the cans. The game plays this 88-tick clip at about double speed (a 44-tick stage). The fighter does not move or turn in the clip; only the hips joint may translate. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s. Tick 0 and tick 88 are his idle pose exactly (image 3).

Feet. Both feet stay where the idle puts them for the whole clip (left forward, right back): this is a lunge on planted feet, not a step. The left foot and both toes stay planted. The right (back) heel may peel up 2-4 cm while he lunges forward, toes staying on the floor, and comes back down in the recovery. Hold the feet with two_bone leg IK after every body edit and check them with ./genra contacts.

Hands. Open, grabbing claws during the reach, fists from the grab on. Open: the fingers curl gently toward the palm (each finger joint bent 15-40 degrees toward the palm), the thumb apart and opposed to the fingers, like a hand about to close on a ball. Closed: fist() on both hands, the thumb across the closed fingers. A finger must never bend backward toward the back of the hand (the old clip did, for 33 ticks); the hinge check must pass on every finger at every key. Wrists stay near the line of the forearm (under about 45 degrees); turn the forearm and elbow, not the wrist.

The move (88 ticks, played once; authored at twice the game length):
- Tick 0: idle exactly.
- Tick 10, the lock-on: he settles a little lower (hips down 1-2 cm), the head dips and the chin tucks as he fixes the target; the fists rise a touch and the fingers start to open.
- Tick 18, the reach: both arms shoot forward and up to grab the target's head: hands open (claws), at least 0.28 m ahead of the hips and up at about the height of his own head at idle (at least 0.28 m above the entry hips), shoulder-width apart (0.22-0.35 m between the hands), palms facing each other and a little down. The weight shifts slightly forward onto the front (left) foot; the chest leans in after the arms; the head is up, chin up, grinning, eyes on the target.
- Tick 24, the grab and the rear-back: the hands snap shut into fists where they were (they have caught the head) and the elbows pull back a little, while the body rears back: the weight rolls onto the back (right) foot, the hips shift back 3-5 cm and drop 2-3 cm, the chest arches back 20-30 degrees from the idle's hunch, the head tips back with the chin up. He is pulling the target toward him while he coils.
- Tick 27, loaded, the tick before the hit (window 28-38): the hips have already started forward (they lead the strike), while the chest and head are still at their furthest back: the head behind the hips (at least 2 cm behind them, front to back) and high. The fists are still out in front at about head height, gripping.
- Tick 33, the strike, mid-drive and fastest: two things meet. The fists yank down and back toward his hips, pulling the caught head down, while the hips lunge forward 8-12 cm and down 4-6 cm over the bent front knee and the chest pitches forward hard, throwing his skull forward and down between his arms. The head is out in front: at least 0.35 m ahead of the hips, at about the height of his own chest at idle, exactly on his centre line (within 4 cm of the middle, left to right).
- Tick 38, impact and follow-through, the end of the hit: the head has driven on, forward and down, to its furthest and lowest: at least 0.36 m ahead of the hips (his spine from hips to head is only 0.39 m, so this is nearly flat) and at least 0.25 m lower than at idle, still on the centre line, and well ahead of both fists (the fists have yanked back to beside his hips, at least 0.15 m behind the head). The body is compressed behind the head: the chest folded forward over the front thigh, the hips at their lowest (6-9 cm down). This is the squash of the impact.
- Tick 50, rebound: he lets go; the head comes back up and back as the hips push back over the middle of the stance; the chest rises toward the idle's hunch; the fists come in to the front of his hips.
- Tick 64, balanced: close to the idle, the weight centred, the back heel down, the fists in front of the hips; only a small difference from idle remains, which settles out by tick 78.
- Tick 88: idle exactly.

Flow. The hips lead every change of direction; the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more. On the way back the head is the last thing to tip back; on the strike the hips start forward while the head is still back, then the skull whips past them while the fists yank the other way. The fingers close fast at the grab (2-3 ticks) and lag the arms a tick on the reach. Keep moving holds, never the same pose twice in a row: the old clip froze for game ticks 10-14 and 35-40. The tail is left at rest: the game's spring trails it from the hips. After the hit, the recovery is plain: he regains balance and the arms take the shortest calm path back to his idle. No gesture, no flourish in the ending.

the head is the hitbox: it must travel fast, forward and down, through the hit window, ending well ahead of him on the centre line
the feet stay planted where the idle has them; the fighter does not move or turn in the clip
adjustable: the owner said the frame data can change: every tick of the clock (88 authored ticks for a proposed 44-tick stage, hit from authored 28 for 10 ticks, IASA 78) may move to suit the motion
how far he rears back and how deep the lunge goes, within the beats above
the reach's height and the yank's path, as long as the arms pull back while the head drives out, and stay clear of the head and jetpack
